display.title: Episode 397: The Strange Pillar of Fire (Vov Tishrei)
display.summary_short: A show for the yahrzeit of the Shpoler Zeide: his own Hop Kozak march, Shema and the Twelve Pesukim with two young guests, the mystery of the pillar of fire, and a listener's letter.
display.summary_long: Broadcast a few days after Rosh Hashanah 5750, just before Vov Tishrei. Uncle Yossi explains that Vov Tishrei is the yahrzeit of the Shpoler Zeide, Rabbi Aryeh Leib ben Boruch, when his many descendants gather to tell his stories and follow his example. The weekly march is the Hop Kozak, a tune composed by the Shpoler Zeide himself. Two girls, one visiting from a shlichus family in Madrid and her pen pal from Brooklyn, lead the Shema and each recites one of the Twelve Pesukim. The story, 'The Strange Pillar of Fire', opens with a fire at the home of the Alter Rebbe and a mysterious spiral of flame rising to the sky. It goes back to the day the Shpoler Zeide read a holy manuscript the Alter Rebbe was writing, the 'Sefer shel Tzaddikim', and begged that it be returned to Heaven because the world was not ready; he wished that his own soul would rise in such a pillar of fire. The book burned in the fire at the very moment the Shpoler Zeide passed away. A mailbox splashdown brings a letter and a tzedakah box drawing from a girl in Williamsburg, and the show closes with candle times for Shabbos Shuvah.
display.lesson: Remember the tzaddikim on their yahrzeit and try to follow their example of Torah and Ahavas Yisroel.

date.note: 'A few days after Rosh Hashanah'; 'this coming Thursday is Vov Tishrei' and 'this coming Shabbos, Shabbos Shuvah' fit Tuesday 4 Tishrei 5750 (3 Oct 1989).

advisories.note: The story ends with the Shpoler Zeide's passing and his town in mourning.
